significance: A Shaiva pilgrimage temple at Medda in Brahmanbaria, built about two centuries ago by the sculptor Durgacharan Acharjee on land given by Noor Muhammad, a landlord of Sarail. Its 28-foot image of Kal Bhairab is claimed to be the largest of its kind, and images of Kali and Parvati stand alongside.
story: The sculptor Durgacharan Acharjee is said to have been moved by a dream to shape the great earthen image of Kal Bhairab.
